analyst_view.overall: Early view: Gladbach are bottom with one league win, have Ko Itakura suspended after his red card in Hamburg, and captain Tim Kleindienst is still working back from a muscle tear under Alexander Blessin, who replaced the sacked Eugen Polanski in September. Dortmund are unbeaten with the league's best defence, but Serhou Guirassy has a thigh strain and Carney Chukwuemeka went off injured against Elversberg. With a Champions League trip to Arsenal three days later, Niko Kovač may rotate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Dortmund's league games average under three goals (16 scored, 7 conceded) and Kovač's side tends to control games rather than chase a big margin, while Gladbach lose Itakura and are likely still without Kleindienst. Gladbach do concede often, which is why I do not go far below the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners split evenly. Dortmund should have more of the ball but have scored only two set-piece goals and often build patiently rather than cross, and Gladbach at home will try to press early. Nothing points clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. I lean slightly higher: Gladbach's frustration has shown in their discipline, with Itakura's second yellow in Hamburg and bookings for throwing the ball away and an arm in an opponent's face against Paderborn. Dortmund collected three yellows even in a routine home win over Elversberg.

shots.text: The site has 28.2 shots, 13.5 for Gladbach. That looks high against the league's tightest defence for a home side likely to be without Kleindienst and relying on Shuto Machino and teenager Wael Mohya. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. With Guirassy doubtful, Dortmund perhaps rotating before Arsenal and Gladbach short of a finisher, I lean a little lower. Felix Nmecha, who scored twice against Elversberg with late runs from midfield, is Dortmund's likeliest source of efforts on target if Guirassy is out.
